title: Recording: Drumming Is My Madness, Stop And Take The Time To Smell The Roses, Back Off Boogaloo by Ringo Starr | 1980
content:
Evergreen Studios, Los Angeles
Producer: Harry Nilsson
Engineer: Rick Riccio

Ringo Starr recorded three songs for his eighth studio album, Stop And Smell The Roses, on 4 November 1980.

‘Drumming Is My Madness’ was written by Harry Nilsson, who had collaborated with Starr since 1973’s Ringo. Nilsson also co-wrote ‘Stop And Take The Time To Smell The Roses’ with Starr, and co-produced both songs as well as a re-recording of ‘Back Off Boogaloo’.

‘Drumming Is My Madness’ is one [of my favourites], because it was fun. It was Harry Nilsson, Jim Keltner and I.
Ringo Starr
Modern Drummer, 19 July 2005

‘Stop And Take The Time To Smell The Roses’ was co-written by Starr and Nilsson. When the album was released on compact disc in 1994 it contained six bonus tracks, including an “original vocal version” of the song.

The day’s final recording was a remake of ‘Back Off Boogaloo’, Starr’s 1972 glam rock hit single.

The new version contained musical snippets from ‘It Don’t Come Easy’, ‘With A Little Help From My Friends’, ‘Good Day Sunshine’, and ‘Baby You’re A Rich Man’, ‘Help!’, and ‘Lady Madonna’.

Further recording took place from 1-5 December at Nassau’s Compass Point Studios. Starr’s lead vocals were laid down on 4 December.

Page last updated: 3 June 2026
